title: Oxnard, CA, Foreclosures Could Soon Unlock Discounted Homes for Buyers - NewsBreak
text:
By The Realtor.com Team ,
7 hours ago
A new report from Realtor.com® is tracking the recent trajectory of foreclosures , shedding light on what happens when these homes become Real Estate Owned (REO) and are listed by banks. This research indicates that the rate of foreclosures has ticked up in recent years after a period of suppression following the COVID-19 pandemic.
However, while the number of foreclosures has increased, the current rate is only about as common as it was in 2019. These levels remain well below what the nation witnessed during the Great Financial Crisis .
Moreover, the report identified specific markets that have seen the most foreclosure listings as of June 2026. Among the areas experiencing a significant uptick is Oxnard, CA , presenting a potential opportunity for prospective buyers in a challenging market.
Oxnard foreclosure listings see an increase In the Oxnard-Thousand Oaks-Ventura, CA, metro area, the foreclosure share of listings was 0.30% as of June 2026. This figure reflects a notable increase in such properties becoming available on the market.
Furthermore, this rise in foreclosures comes at a time when the median listing price for all homes in the area stands at $984,735. For buyers struggling with affordability, the foreclosure market may offer a pathway to homeownership.
As a result, these properties can represent a significant value. In April 2026, the median foreclosed home was sold for a discount of 27.2% from its Realtor.com automated valuation models (AVM).
Understanding the national foreclosure trend The recent rise of foreclosures follows a period of historic lows. During the COVID-19 pandemic, defaults plummeted due to several key federal provisions that helped homeowners remain in their properties.
However, with those provisions expired, the numbers have climbed. As of the start of 2026, the national foreclosure start rate stood at 0.24%, roughly matching the 2019 benchmark, according to Mortgage Bankers Association data reported by Moody's . This trend is a symptom of the affordability crisis affecting the housing market.
“Buyers since 2023, when home prices flattened off, are most at risk. They’re newer to their mortgage and don’t have as much of an equity stake in their home, partly because the first few years of mortgage payments are made up of significantly more interest than principal and partly because their home has not appreciated as much as those that were purchased before the price surge of 2021 and 2022,” said Joel Berner , senior economist, Realtor.com.
Berner added, “The affordability advantages of these metros that made homeownership possible for buyers on the margin lead to a selection bias that leaves the typical homeowner more susceptible to foreclosure.” While these homes offer a lower price point, they often come with risks.
“The biggest risk is that many of these homes have been vacant or neglected. In our climate, that can mean moisture issues, mold, deferred maintenance, storm-related repairs, or other problems that aren't immediately visible,” said Danette McManus , a local real estate agent in Lake Charles, LA , which currently leads the nation with foreclosures .
